_comment: Timing-coupled sites in the Go test suite that scripts/check_test_flakiness.py
has seen and that are ACCEPTED. The checker fails on any site not listed here,
and equally on any entry here that no longer matches a site -- a stale
allowance is how a ban quietly stops applying.
Keyed on file + enclosing symbol rather than line number: a line number goes
stale on any edit above it, and a ledger that must be renumbered to stay valid
is a ledger people delete entries from.
Every entry below is bucket (c), CONTAINER RETRY -- see docs/60-test-flakiness.md.
Buckets (a) BOUNDED POLL and (b) BARE SLEEP-THEN-ASSERT are absent for opposite
reasons: (a) is not flagged at all because a deadline-guarded poll is the
correct shape, and (b) is empty because the three sites that had it were
rewritten onto internal/testsupport.StaysFalse rather than recorded.

accepted.reason: Backs off against a real SQL Server that is still booting, inside `for i := 0; i < 60`. The wait is for a socket that is not yet listening, so a shorter interval would only poll a closed port faster. Bounded by iteration count; the test is skipped entirely without WAREHOUSE_MSSQL_DSN.
Same SQL Server cold start, wrapped in an `exec` helper that retries each statement up to 60 times. Bounded by iteration count.
Two sites (the GROUP BY and its rows.Err retry), both inside `for i := 0; i < 60`. Delta reflection runs against the real engine, so the retry covers both container start and the reflection landing.
The first relayed statement may arrive before SQL Server accepts connections; retried up to 60 times. Bounded by iteration count.

Establishes the non-strict baseline before asserting on the strict refusal -- a connection error here would be indistinguishable from SQL Server rejecting the statement, which is what the test is about. Bounded by iteration count.
CREATE TABLE against the warehouse surface, retried for cold start up to 60 times. Bounded by iteration count.
